## Historical audit — S0337

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/test/bw_0005/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file. The supplied observations contain no split lines.

**Goal versus inference:** The explicit task was to reconstruct an indoor RGB reference with separate editable meshes and matching camera and framing. H interpreted the image as a classroom inset; that scene interpretation and its estimated bounds are H’s claims, not independently inspected image evidence (line 1, `model_request`; line 3, H `model_response`).

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Lines 3–4, H response and step 1 `execute` | Built multiple named assets: walls, floor, windows, four cabinets, table, stools, rug, trays and blocks. Cabinet shelves, backs and uprights are separate child meshes; coordinates specify their placement, not independent proof of correct physical connection. Colors and floor seams approximate surfaces; no texture maps are evident. No articulated figure or pose is represented. |
| Lines 6, 8–10, step 1 completion/result/selection | Build and render completed successfully. The printed upper-left window estimate `(0.12, 0.10)` versus projection `(0.436, 0.205)` shows a numerical discrepancy, conditional on the estimated correspondence—not visual calibration. |
| Lines 11 and 13–14, H request, response and step 2 execution | H received the reference, render and a request to compare them. H reported an exterior wall obstruction, gray margins and undersized foreground; these are its visual assessments. It changed camera position, target and lens, enlarged/repositioned elements and altered colors and lights. A small upward-aim trial was computed and restored, but it was not a before/after test of the major camera change. |
| Lines 19–20, step 2 result/selection | Build and render succeeded. Trial projections moved downward as expected; selected-camera window and island projections still differed from H’s reference estimates. Projection alone does not establish visibility or silhouette. |
| Lines 23–24, 26, 28–30, H response and step 3 execution/result/selection | H reported gray space above walls and low cubby contrast. It extended the room, added a ceiling, shifted the island and rug left, darkened backs and reduced lighting while retaining camera pose. Build and render succeeded and step 3 was selected. Its final projected island left was `(0.458, 0.722)` against H’s estimated `(0.34, 0.49)` (line 29). |

**Input and autonomy:** No separately identified teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update or teacher-authored patch appears in this student trajectory; teacher receipt or adoption cannot be established. The explicit review prompts and rendered images were supplied to H (lines 11 and 21). H independently interpreted those inputs and authored revisions; its recorded CLI sessions show no external tool calls (lines 2, 12, 22).

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Three executions and renders formally succeeded; this is not evidence of a correct reconstruction. The final image is not visible in the supplied text, and no final visual review or independent geometric validation is recorded. Whether the ceiling, lighting, object coverage, material appearance, connections and framing improved remains unknown. The numerical mismatches are consistent with remaining alignment problems but cannot identify their cause.

**Lessons:** Transferably, separate projected landmarks from visible contours and distinguish lighting from surface color. Task-specifically, H’s inset interpretation, classroom inventory and ceiling correction remain hypotheses; neither their accuracy nor the final visual match is established.
